## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dhātuvivaṇṇapetavatthu* ("Insulting the Worship of Relics", Pv 35) is a verse story preserved within the *Petavatthu* in the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The narrative centers on the karmic consequences of denigrating relic veneration, teaching that insulting those who worship the Buddha's bodily relics leads to severe suffering in the realm of the petas [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral indexes translations of the text across five modern languages [SuttaCentral].
No separate historical parallels in other early Buddhist canons are registered in curated collections, but DharmaNexus identifies extensive textual reuse between the verses of the text and its commentary, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (comprising 32 shared segments, spanning §§1.1–10.4) [DharmaNexus]. Additionally, DharmaNexus identifies machine alignments with Tibetan canonical literature, including sections of the *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155) and the *Śrāvakabhūmi* within the *Yogācārabhūmi* (D4036), though these represent automated algorithmic similarities rather than verified parallels [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
